verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a community report that a Mac can be reached via Remote Desktop after enabling macOS's built-in Remote Management. That implies the OS can share its desktop for remote control, but it is a single thin mention in a thread about an authentication bug. iPhone Mirroring, Sidecar and Universal Control are local device-continuity features, not remote desktop sessions, so they earn no credit. missing for 10: first-party docs for Screen Sharing/Remote Management, evidence of initiating outbound remote desktop sessions from the Mac, details on setup, protocols (e.g. VNC) and remote/internet access.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can share my desktop remotely or access a remote desktop session from my machine

citations.quote: After turning on Remote Management on a second Mac, a user could log into it via Remote Desktop as root with no password
